title: Protocol for Extracting Amynthas Species Cocoons
author: Maryam Nouri-Aiin

steps.title: Prepare Sieves
steps.instruction: Set up the sieving apparatus using Sieve No. 12 (standard size for cocoons 2.5 ± 0.05mm to 4.5 ± 0.05mm) or Sieve No. 14 (1.4mm).

substeps.instruction: Optionally stack Sieve No. 8 on top of Sieve No. 12 to remove large debris like wood fragments and roots.
If using Sieve No. 8, ensure it is stacked on Sieve No. 12 to prevent cocoon loss.

steps.title: Load Soil Sample
steps.instruction: Place approximately one cup of soil into Sieve No. 8 (if stacked) or Sieve No. 12.

steps.title: Initial Soil Wash
steps.instruction: Submerge the sieves in a bin of water, ensuring the water level covers the soil but does not fully submerge the sieve.

substeps.instruction: Gently rub the soil to break down larger particles, allowing soil to pass through Sieve No. 8 onto Sieve No. 12.

steps.title: Remove Coarse Debris
steps.instruction: Remove Sieve No. 8 and the retained debris from the setup.

steps.title: Secondary Soil Wash
steps.instruction: Lift Sieve No. 12 so that water covers the soil but does not submerge it.

substeps.instruction: Gently rub the soil against the sieve to separate remaining particles, avoiding excessive pressure to prevent breaking cocoons.

steps.title: Final Rinse
steps.instruction: Perform a final rinse of the contents in a second bin filled with clean water.

steps.title: Extract and Identify Cocoons
steps.instruction: Extract cocoons using forceps, potentially using a white background or a stereo microscope to improve visibility.

substeps.instruction: Distinguish cocoons from seeds/soil by applying gentle pressure; cocoons are elastic and bouncy, while seeds/soil break apart.
Verify species by size: Amynthas tokioensis (~2.5 ± 0.05mm), Amynthas agrestis (~3.5 ± 0.05mm), or Amynthas hilgendorfi (~4.5 ± 0.05mm).
Use molecular identification methods for specimens falling between species size ranges.

steps.title: Store Cocoons
steps.instruction: Place extracted cocoons in a petri dish filled with water to prevent dehydration.
